title: State of Bihar through CBI v. Rajesh Ranjan @ Pappu Yadav (Ajit Sarkar Murder)
crime_type: Contract Political Homicide / AK-47 Drive-By Ambush / Criminal-Political Nexus
court_or_authority: Supreme Court of India / High Court of Judicature at Patna
source: Patna High Court Judgment & Indian Kanoon
evidence: 107 empty cartridges of automatic 7.62mm AK-47 ammunition recovered from politician vehicle at railway crossing
Testimony of injured personal assistant and driver surviving the barrage of automatic fire
Disclosures of contract hitman Rajan Tiwari regarding conspiracy meetings at Patna guest house
Inter-state ballistic tracking of military-grade contraband rifles smuggled across Nepal border
modus_operandi: Ambushed communist trade union leader and sitting MLA Ajit Sarkar while his vehicle slowed at a railway crossing. Multiple motorcycle-borne shooters armed with AK-47 rifles blocked the road and pumped over 100 rounds into the vehicle, killing Sarkar, his driver, and bodyguard instantaneously.
personality_disorder: Feudal muscle hegemony, political territorial ruthlessness, and normalized contract violence.
common_traits: Drive-by automatic weapon ambush at transit chokepoints
Overwhelming firepower (100+ rounds) to guarantee lethality
Contract enforcers recruited from cross-border districts
Long trial duration characterized by witness intimidation
summary: Defining case of Indian political mafia violence in the 1990s. Investigated by CBI, resulting in landmark Supreme Court orders transferring Pappu Yadav from Beur Jail to Tihar Jail to prevent unlawful political gatherings inside prison.
